blocks.markdown: ProximalBase.jl supplies mathematical functions and array-like iterates for optimization. Its organization is easiest to read in three layers: **function types describe the objective, traits describe available operations, and iterate types describe the coordinates being updated.** Solvers sit above this interface and call its operations.
# Organization at a glance

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[External solver] --> O[Generic operations]
  O --> F[Concrete function methods]
  O --> I[Array or iterate methods]
  F --> W[Wrapped functions and numerical workspaces]
  T[Traits describe capabilities] -.-> S
```

| Layer | Main names | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Function root | `AbstractFunction` | Callable objective terms and common operation interface |
| Scalar separability | `SeparableFunction` | Build array operations from scalar value and proximal kernels |
| Group structure | `AbstractGroupPenalty`, `HomogeneousGroupNorm` | Shared grouping machinery and group updates |
| Observation losses | `ScalarLoss`, contained in `GLMLoss` | Loss and derivatives for one observation |
| Function composition | `Scaled`, `Sum`, `Constrained`, `Spectral`, and others | Store functions and delegate operations |
| Iterates | `SparseIterate`, `SymmetricSparseIterate`, `AtomIterate` | Store coefficients and expose scalar or group coordinates |
# The inheritance tree
Solid arrows below mean “is a subtype of,” directed from subtype to supertype. The concrete examples are representative.

```mermaid
flowchart BT
  SEP[SeparableFunction] --> AF[AbstractFunction]
  GP[AbstractGroupPenalty] --> AF
  HGN[HomogeneousGroupNorm] --> GP
  L1[NormL1 and ElasticNet] --> SEP
  GN[GroupNormL2 and GroupNormLinf and SparseGroupNormL2] --> HGN
  NC[GroupMCP and GroupSCAD] --> GP
  DIRECT[LeastSquaresLoss and GLMLoss and Sum and Spectral] --> AF
  OBS[Logistic and Poisson and Huber] --> SL[ScalarLoss]
  SI[SparseIterate] --> AA[AbstractArray]
  SSI[SymmetricSparseIterate] --> AM[AbstractMatrix]
  AI[AtomIterate] --> AV[AbstractVector]
```
`ScalarLoss` is a separate root. `GLMLoss` contains a scalar loss; it does not inherit from it. The three iterate types inherit from Julia array abstractions and are independent of the function tree.
# Traits are capabilities

| Query | Meaning | Operations a caller can use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issmooth(f)` | Differentiable on the interior of its domain | `gradient!`, `value_and_gradient!` |
| `isproximable(f)` | Provides a proximal operator | `prox!`, `value_and_prox!` |
| `isseparable(f)` | Sum over individual entries | `prox_entry`, coordinate update machinery |
| `isconvex(f)` | Convexity | Select applicable algorithmic guarantees |
| `hashessian(f)` | Provides second order oracles | `hessian_vec!`, `quadratic_model` |
| `iszeropreserving(f)` | Scalar value at zero is zero and scalar prox preserves zero | Skip implicit zeros on supported sparse paths |

The first five queries default to false on `AbstractFunction` and are generally declared on types. `iszeropreserving` is an instance property for separable functions because parameters such as box bounds can change it. Traits describe support; Julia dispatch selects the actual method from the argument types. Smoothness does not promise a finite global Lipschitz constant.
# Who calls whom

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant S as Solver
  participant L as Smooth function f
  participant P as Penalty g
  participant K as Scalar kernel
  S->>L: gradient!(grad, f, x)
  L-->>S: gradient buffer
  Note over S: v = x - gamma * grad
  S->>P: prox!(next, g, v, gamma)
  opt g uses SeparableFunction implementation
    P->>K: prox_entry(g, v[i], i, gamma)
    K-->>P: updated entry
  end
  P-->>S: next iterate
```

A coordinate solver instead calls `prox_coordinate!(x, g, k, γ)`. For a separable function this delegates to `prox_entry`; for a matching group penalty and `AtomIterate`, it applies a group kernel. A Newton caller asks for Hessian products or a quadratic model. The optimization loop owns the step selection, iteration, and stopping decisions.

2. [SeparableFunction and scalar kernels](https://chatgpt.com/space/page_0d1da0aa24548191bcf6c74c7c5a9b6e)
3. [AbstractGroupPenalty and HomogeneousGroupNorm](https://chatgpt.com/space/page_7c673b96f0c48191923f1eee9bf0cd27)
4. [ScalarLoss and its composition into GLMLoss](https://chatgpt.com/space/page_d31a54e6b19881918c2ce1a321911b0a)
5. [Function wrappers iterates and workspaces](https://chatgpt.com/space/page_98a0214de41c8191a6400d69d863833c)

title: AbstractFunction and the common operation interface

blocks.markdown: [Package overview](https://chatgpt.com/space/page_19d0374c8de481918344267237028f43)
`AbstractFunction` is the root for objective terms: losses, penalties, set indicators, and wrappers. A value such as `NormL1(λ)` is a callable object; `f(x)` evaluates the term.
# Contract

| Role | Implement | Common fallback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Any function | `(f::MyFunction)(x)` | Value is `Inf` outside the domain |
| Smooth function | `value_and_gradient!(g, f, x)` and smoothness trait | `gradient!` calls the combined method; allocating helpers build buffers |
| Proximable function | `prox!(y, f, x, γ)` and proximability trait | `prox` allocates an output; `value_and_prox!` applies prox then evaluates its result |
| Second order function | Hessian products and quadratic model methods with `hashessian` | `hessian_vec` allocates its output |

These are generic functions with methods selected by multiple dispatch. Read `prox!(y, f, x, γ)` as an operation on a function and two arrays, rather than a member method of `f`. Mutating operations take the output first.
# Representative direct subtypes

`LeastSquaresLoss`, `QuadraticFunction`, `SqrNormL2`, `GLMLoss`, `LogDetLoss`, `NormL2`, `IndSimplex`, `NuclearNorm`, and wrappers all directly subtype this root. There is no separate abstract smooth-function or indicator-function superclass. The private `_isindicator` trait identifies indicator behavior.

`SqrNormL2`, `QuadraticFunction`, `LeastSquaresLoss`, and `LogDetLoss` are both smooth and proximable. `SqrNormL2` is mathematically separable and declares that trait while directly inheriting from `AbstractFunction`: separability as a capability is broader than membership in `SeparableFunction`.
# Additional operations

`lipschitz` supplies a known global gradient bound, which may be infinite; smoothness alone does not supply a finite bound. `coordinate_lipschitz` supplies coordinate curvature information. `restrict(f, S)` constructs a supported restriction for active-set work and may drop an additive constant. `gradient_mapping!` calls the smooth gradient and penalty prox to compute a stopping quantity.
# Source

[Common interface](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/interface.jl) and [Second order operations](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/second_order.jl).
[Package overview](https://chatgpt.com/space/page_19d0374c8de481918344267237028f43)

`SeparableFunction <: AbstractFunction` is the implementation shortcut for functions that sum scalar terms over array entries. Supply two small scalar kernels and reuse the array and sparse-iterate machinery.
# What a subtype supplies

```julia
struct WeightedSquare <: SeparableFunction
    w::Vector{Float64}
end
ProximalBase.value_entry(f::WeightedSquare, v, i) = f.w[i] * v^2 / 2
ProximalBase.prox_entry(f::WeightedSquare, v, i, γ) = v / (1 + γ * f.w[i])
ProximalBase.isconvex(::Type{WeightedSquare}) = true
ProximalBase.iszeropreserving(::WeightedSquare) = true
```

Here `i` is a linear entry index, allowing weights and bounds to vary by entry. Inheritance supplies `isseparable = true` and `isproximable = true`. Convexity and smoothness remain separate declarations and require their corresponding methods.
# Who calls whom

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  V[Array value f x] --> VE[value_entry for each entry]
  P[Array prox!] --> PE[prox_entry for each entry]
  VP[value_and_prox!] --> PE
  VP --> VE
  C[prox_coordinate!] --> PE
  Z[iszeropreserving] -.-> SP[Stored entries only on supported sparse paths]
```

`value_and_prox!` evaluates scalar values at the updated entries. Specialized methods can fuse work further. Zero preservation means both `fᵢ(0) = 0` and `prox_entry(f, 0, i, γ) = 0`; it lets sparse paths skip implicit zeros.
# Concrete families

| Family | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Convex penalties | `NormL1`, `NormL1Nonneg`, `ElasticNet` |
| Nonconvex penalties | `NormL0`, `MCP`, `SCAD`, `CappedL1`, `LogPenalty`, `NormLq` |
| Entrywise sets | `IndBox`, `IndNonnegative`, `IndPattern`, `IndBanded` |
| Losses and domain terms | `CheckLoss`, `HingeLoss`, `EpsInsensitiveLoss`, `NegEntropy`, `KLDivergence`, `NegLog`, `Berhu` |
`SeparableSum` is a different abstraction: it acts on a tuple of blocks and directly subtypes `AbstractFunction`. A group penalty couples entries within a group and belongs to the group hierarchy.
# Source

[Scalar kernels and reusable loops](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/functions/separable.jl), [Coordinate dispatch](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/interface.jl), and [Diagonal step methods](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/metric.jl).
[Package overview](https://chatgpt.com/space/page_19d0374c8de481918344267237028f43)
Group penalties share grouping and active-set machinery. Their hierarchy separates the common structure from the stronger properties of convex, positively homogeneous norms.
# Inheritance

```mermaid
flowchart BT
  G2[GroupNormL2] --> H[HomogeneousGroupNorm]
  GI[GroupNormLinf] --> H
  SG[SparseGroupNormL2] --> H
  H --> G[AbstractGroupPenalty]
  M[GroupMCP] --> G
  S[GroupSCAD] --> G
  G --> A[AbstractFunction]
```

`AbstractGroupPenalty` supplies the proximability trait. `HomogeneousGroupNorm` also supplies convexity. These abstract names are internal or qualified interfaces rather than exported entry points. `AbstractGroupNorm` is a compatibility alias for `AbstractGroupPenalty`; despite its name, it includes nonconvex group penalties.
# Shared structure and calls

Concrete group penalties retain groups, weights, and index mappings. Full proximal calls apply kernels to groups. For an `AtomIterate` with matching groups, `prox_coordinate!(x, g, k, γ)` updates group `k`, and `kkt_violation(g, grad, x, k)` measures violation for a group at zero. Group-specific methods select the kernel through dispatch.

`AtomIterate(x, g)` aligns the iterate with a penalty's grouping. The iterate groups partition the vector; entries left unpenalized by the penalty receive their own free grouping. Shared groups allow supported sparse operations to visit only active groups.
# The useful distinction

`NormL1` separates by entry; `GroupNormL2` separates across groups but couples entries within each group. `GroupMCP` and `GroupSCAD` reuse grouping while requiring nonconvex kernels. A caller that needs a homogeneous convex group norm must use the narrower abstraction.
`IndBallGroupL0` is a related group constraint but directly subtypes `AbstractFunction`, so it is not a descendant of `AbstractGroupPenalty`.
# Source

[Group hierarchy and kernels](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/functions/norms.jl), [Sparse group norm](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/functions/sparsegroup.jl), [Nonconvex group penalties](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/functions/nonconvex.jl), and [Grouped iterate](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/atom_iterate.jl).

title: ScalarLoss and its composition into GLMLoss

blocks.markdown: [Package overview](https://chatgpt.com/space/page_19d0374c8de481918344267237028f43)

`ScalarLoss` describes the loss of one observation as a function of a scalar predictor. It is a separate abstract root. `GLMLoss <: AbstractFunction` contains a scalar loss, design matrix, response, weights, offset, and working buffers.
# Contract and concrete types

| Operation | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `loss(η, y)` | Value for one observation |
| `deriv(loss, η, y)` | First derivative in the predictor |
| `deriv2(loss, η, y)` | Second derivative in the predictor |
| `curvature(loss)` | Global bound on second derivative, possibly `Inf` |
| `value_and_deriv(loss, η, y)` | Combined calculation; default calls value and derivative |

Concrete types include `Squared`, `Logistic`, `Poisson`, `Huber`, `SquaredHinge`, `SmoothCheck`, `ConvolutionCheck`, and `Smoothed`. These scalar names and `ScalarLoss` are accessed with the `ProximalBase` qualifier.
# Who calls whom

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  C[Solver gradient call] --> G[GLMLoss]
  G --> X[Compute predictor X beta plus offset]
  X --> L[ScalarLoss value_and_deriv per observation]
  L --> W[Apply observation weights]
  W --> R[Multiply by transpose of X]
  N[Hessian or quadratic model call] --> D[ScalarLoss deriv2 per observation]
```
`LogisticLoss`, `PoissonLoss`, and `HuberLoss` are aliases for specializations of `GLMLoss`, with convenience constructors. They are not sibling classes that inherit from `GLMLoss`.
# Connection to second order methods

`GLMLoss` uses scalar second derivatives for Hessian products and an IRLS quadratic model. Its model is another `GLMLoss` with a `Squared` scalar loss and working responses and weights. The implementation floors observation curvature at a small positive value where needed for finite working responses; this is the implemented model rather than an exact Hessian model at zero curvature.
Adding a scalar observation loss can reuse the design-matrix calculations in `GLMLoss`. Adding an unrelated objective term instead starts from `AbstractFunction` or `SeparableFunction`.
# Source

[ScalarLoss and GLMLoss](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/functions/glm.jl), [Additional scalar loss types](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/functions/losses.jl), [Smoothed scalar losses](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/envelope.jl), and [IRLS model construction](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/second_order.jl).
[Package overview](https://chatgpt.com/space/page_19d0374c8de481918344267237028f43)

Wrappers assemble functions through composition. Iterates supply array storage and coordinate meaning. Workspaces retain numerical buffers inside functions. These are three different relationships from inheritance.
# Wrappers contain other functions

| Wrapper | Meaning and delegation |
| --- | --- |
| `Scaled`, `Tilt`, `Translate` | Scale a function, add a linear term, or shift its input; transform and call the inner operations |
| `Conjugate` | Uses the inner prox through Moreau decomposition; constructor requires convexity |
| `Sum` | Add functions on the same input; add their gradients when smooth; no generic prox of the sum |
| `SeparableSum` | Apply functions to separate tuple blocks; prox and gradients act block by block |
| `SliceSum`, `FiberSum` | Apply functions along slices or fibers of an array |
| `Precompose` | Apply an inner function after a linear map; the matrix construction requires `A A′ = μ I` |
| `Regularize` | Add a quadratic ridge term |
| `MoreauEnvelope` | Build a smooth envelope from a convex proximable function |
| `Spectral`, `SingularValue` | Decompose a matrix, call an inner vector prox on eigenvalues or singular values, reconstruct |

Each wrapper is itself an `AbstractFunction`. Trait methods propagate the supported capabilities under the wrapper's conditions. A wrapper can report separability without inheriting from `SeparableFunction`. `Spectral` requires permutation invariance; `SingularValue` requires absolute symmetry, with additional conditions for its nonconvex construction.

`Constrained` is a generic constructor function, rather than an abstract or concrete type. Supported combinations select implementations such as `BoxConstrained`, `LinearConstrained`, `BallConstrained`, `SphereConstrained`, and `AffineConstrained`.
# Iterates form a separate array hierarchy

| Type | Julia parent | One coordinate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SparseIterate{T,N}` | `AbstractArray{T,N}` | One array entry |
| `SymmetricSparseIterate{T}` | `AbstractMatrix{T}` | One lower triangular entry representing a symmetric pair off the diagonal |
| `AtomIterate{T}` | `AbstractVector{T}` | One group of entries |

`ncoordinates`, `coordinates`, `activecoordinates`, `activate!`, and `isactive` expose coordinate and active-set structure. `atom` gives a group view. A separable function's `prox_entry` still uses a full linear array index; a symmetric iterate translates its lower triangular coordinate index before the call.
# Workspaces are owned numerical state

Losses and wrappers can own scratch arrays, cached factorizations, and LAPACK workspaces even when their outer struct is immutable. For example, `GLMLoss` retains predictor and derivative buffers; `Spectral` owns an eigensolver workspace. Workspace types support numerical calculations and do not belong to the objective-function hierarchy.

After changing retained least-squares or quadratic data in place, call `reset_cache!` on the outermost function. It descends through supported wrappers. Keep dimensions unchanged; reconstruct `IndAffine` after changing its data. Give each thread its own function copy when a function owns mutable workspaces.
# Source

[Basic wrappers](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/calculus.jl), [Composition](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/composition.jl), [Constrained constructors](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/constrained.jl), [Sparse iterates](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/sparse_iterate.jl), [AtomIterate](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/atom_iterate.jl), and [Cache lifecycle](https://github.com/mlakolar/ProximalBase.jl/blob/37d32e1579a1cb04a6ef26a175d2858ddd68e8ea/src/caches.jl).
